title: first-principles: is a catapult a viable orbital launch method

messages.content: what if we ignore the haters and use a giant catapult to launch stuff into orbit instead of rockets?! catapult to mars!!!!

An interesting idea! A catapult, or more accurately a mass driver, could theoretically launch payloads into orbit. However, the main challenges are achieving sufficient velocity and managing g-forces. You'd need to reach about 7.8 km/s for low Earth orbit, which means subjecting payloads to extremely high accelerations over a short distance. This might cause structural damage unless the launch system is incredibly long to reduce the g-forces. The atmospheric drag at those speeds is also a serious challenge.
how bad are the g-forces really?! give me a number that’ll make my head spin!!

To reach orbital velocity over a manageable distance of, say, 1 kilometer, you'd experience accelerations well over 1,000 g. For comparison, humans typically pass out around 9 g. You'd need specialized payloads and potentially explosive-resistant containers to withstand those forces. The engineering challenges are immense, but not impossible with enough resources.
so renata will hate this but... it would look cool right?! picture it: mars catapult with flames!!!

Visually, it would indeed be spectacular. Imagine the immense structure arcing through the sky, with flames and sparks flying as the payload accelerates down the track. It would be a breathtaking display of engineering might and ambition. However, flames might not be the most practical element since the primary propulsion is electromagnetic, but they’d definitely add drama. Better keep Dr. Renata Voss in the loop—she’ll make sure it stays grounded in reality.
ok ok what if we add flamethrowers just for show?? and maybe some fireworks at launch!!

Adding flamethrowers and fireworks would certainly create a more dramatic and visually impressive spectacle! While it wouldn't contribute to the actual launch, it could make for an unforgettable event. Just ensure the safety protocols are incredibly robust, and remember to run any plans past Dr. Renata Voss and the safety team. We'll need their expertise to keep the engineering solid while indulging in some theatrical flair.
